findings.issue_text: packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts:176 — [P2, confidence 100] `where: { credentialId: { in: credentialIds } }` counts expired rows that `getCachedAvailability` rejects, so users see a cache timestamp and deletion action indefinitely when the credential has no usable cache.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1024 — [P3 advisory, confidence 75] `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` adds a second cache-freshness representation that the status reader never consumes and an empty update does not advance Prisma `@updatedAt`, so this branch and the added SelectedCalendar fields/repository API are unnecessary places for future cache-status changes to drift.

packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:72 — [P2, confidence 75] `const hasCache = isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt;` suppresses the entire cache-status UI when a Google credential has no cache row (including immediately after deletion), so the feature fails to report the "not cached" state to users who most need status visibility.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:13 — [P1, confidence 100] `export const deleteCacheHandler = async ({ ctx, input }: DeleteCacheOptions) => {` adds destructive, ownership-scoped behavior with no corresponding test in the diff, leaving the required success, unauthorized-credential, and already-empty-cache acceptance paths unverified; a regression can delete the wrong cache or return success without the contract being exercised.

scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:5 — [P1, confidence 100] `ENV_FILE="../.env"` resolves relative to the caller's working directory, so the normal repository-root invocation writes the webhook URL into the parent directory instead of the application's root `.env` and the running app never receives the setting.

scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:35 — [P1, confidence 100] `tmole $TM_PORT > "$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 &` invokes an undeclared global executable, so a clean checkout without a separately installed Tunnelmole binary fails to create the tunnel and exits without configuring webhooks.

apps/web/package.json:11 — [P2, confidence 75] `"dev:cron": "npx tsx cron-tester.ts"` invokes `tsx` even though no workspace package declares it, so offline and install-restricted development environments cannot run the committed cron command and `npx` otherwise executes an unpinned downloaded version outside the lockfile.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:25 — [P1, confidence 100] `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied");` converts an absent or unauthorized credential into an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR/500 instead of the 4xx response the client operation requires.

scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:17 — [P2, confidence 100] `exit 0` makes the explicit tunnel rate-limit and missing-URL failure paths invoked through `cleanup` report success to callers, so automation continues with no usable webhook URL.

apps/web/package.json:11 — P2, confidence 100: Changing `"dev:cron": "ts-node cron-tester.ts"` to `"dev:cron": "npx tsx cron-tester.ts"` alters an unrelated cron-development workflow in a task scoped to calendar-cache status and actions, so this change ships unreviewed dependency/execution behavior with no traceability to the stated intent.

scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:1 — P2, confidence 100: Adding `#!/bin/bash` and a 79-line Tunnelmole/`.env` mutation utility expands the calendar-cache UI/API task into unrelated webhook-development tooling, exposing maintainers to a new environment-changing script that no stated requirement or acceptance criterion justifies.

apps/web/package.json:11 — [P2, confidence 75] `"dev:cron": "npx tsx cron-tester.ts"` executes an undeclared, unpinned package fetched from the npm registry, so a compromised or malicious latest `tsx` release gains arbitrary code execution on a developer machine when this script is run.

scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:79 — [P1, confidence 100] The purported webhook test ends with only `wait "$TMOLE_PID"` and never invokes or asserts the changed cache-status or cache-deletion behavior, so it stays green or blocks identically when the feature is broken and gives reviewers false verification confidence.

goldens.comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems

Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts:176 — [P2, confidence 100] `where: { credentialId: { in: credentialIds } }` counts expired rows that `getCachedAvailability` rejects, so users see a cache timestamp and deletion action indefinitely when the credential has no usable cache.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that getCacheStatusByCredentialIds in calendar-cache.repository.ts queries CalendarCache without filtering by expiresAt, while getCachedAvailability (shown at line 80-95 in the same file) filters with 'expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }'. This means the cache status shown to users via the dropdown will include expired cache entries, showing a 'last updated' timestamp and delete action even when there's no usable (non-expired) cache data. This is a real inconsistency between what's displayed and what's actually functional.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:72 — [P2, confidence 75] `const hasCache = isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt;` suppresses the entire cache-status UI when a Google credential has no cache row (including immediately after deletion), so the feature fails to report the "not cached" state to users who most need status visibility.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims this is a defect because users can't see 'not cached' state. However, looking at the diff, this appears to be intentional design - the dropdown only shows cache-related options when there IS cache data to display/delete. When there's no cache, there's nothing to show or delete. The component still shows disconnect options when applicable (canDisconnect). This is a reasonable UX choice, not a bug - showing 'no cache' status for every non-cached credential would add noise. The finding mischaracterizes intentional behavior as a defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:13 — [P1, confidence 100] `export const deleteCacheHandler = async ({ ctx, input }: DeleteCacheOptions) => {` adds destructive, ownership-scoped behavior with no corresponding test in the diff, leaving the required success, unauthorized-credential, and already-empty-cache acceptance paths unverified; a regression can delete the wrong cache or return success without the contract being exercised.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new deleteCache.handler.ts with ownership-scoped deletion logic (checking credential belongs to user before deleting cache). This is non-trivial business logic that handles authorization and data deletion. The finding correctly identifies that no test file is added in this diff for this new handler. While the code appears correct, the lack of tests for a destructive operation with authorization checks is a legitimate review concern - not a bug, but an important gap for new functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:5 — [P1, confidence 100] `ENV_FILE="../.env"` resolves relative to the caller's working directory, so the normal repository-root invocation writes the webhook URL into the parent directory instead of the application's root `.env` and the running app never receives the setting.

adjudication.rationale: The script uses `ENV_FILE="../.env"` which is a relative path. When the script is executed from the repository root (e.g., `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`), the path `../` resolves to the parent of the repository, not the repository root where the actual `.env` file should be. This means the webhook URL would be written to the wrong location. The script should use `$SCRIPT_DIR/../.env` or an absolute path based on the script's location to correctly target the repository's `.env` file.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:35 — [P1, confidence 100] `tmole $TM_PORT > "$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 &` invokes an undeclared global executable, so a clean checkout without a separately installed Tunnelmole binary fails to create the tunnel and exits without configuring webhooks.

adjudication.rationale: The script does invoke 'tmole' as an external command without checking if it's installed or documenting the dependency. However, this is a developer utility script (in scripts/ directory) for testing Google Calendar webhooks locally, not production code. The script failing when tmole isn't installed is expected behavior for a development tool - it's not a 'bug' in the sense of broken functionality, but rather a missing dependency check or documentation. The finding is valid but overstates severity - a helper script not working without its dependencies installed is a documentation/usability issue, not a defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/package.json:11 — [P2, confidence 75] `"dev:cron": "npx tsx cron-tester.ts"` invokes `tsx` even though no workspace package declares it, so offline and install-restricted development environments cannot run the committed cron command and `npx` otherwise executes an unpinned downloaded version outside the lockfile.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows changing from 'ts-node cron-tester.ts' to 'npx tsx cron-tester.ts'. The finding correctly identifies that using 'npx tsx' will download tsx on-the-fly if not installed, which means: 1) it won't work offline, 2) the version is unpinned and outside the lockfile. This is a legitimate concern about reproducibility and offline development capability. However, this is a dev script, not production code, so it's not a bug but rather an important architectural/tooling concern. The finding is accurate and grounded in the actual diff change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:17 — [P2, confidence 100] `exit 0` makes the explicit tunnel rate-limit and missing-URL failure paths invoked through `cleanup` report success to callers, so automation continues with no usable webhook URL.

adjudication.rationale: The cleanup function at line 17 always calls `exit 0`, which indicates success. When cleanup is called from the rate-limit error path (line 47) or the missing URL path (line 55), the script exits with status 0 despite having failed. This means any automation or CI calling this script would incorrectly believe it succeeded when it actually failed to establish a working webhook URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/package.json:11 — P2, confidence 100: Changing `"dev:cron": "ts-node cron-tester.ts"` to `"dev:cron": "npx tsx cron-tester.ts"` alters an unrelated cron-development workflow in a task scoped to calendar-cache status and actions, so this change ships unreviewed dependency/execution behavior with no traceability to the stated intent.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims this change is 'unrelated' and 'ships unreviewed dependency/execution behavior with no traceability.' However, changing from ts-node to tsx is a legitimate tooling update that appears alongside other changes in the same PR. The change from ts-node to npx tsx is a common migration pattern (tsx is a faster TypeScript executor). This is not a bug - it's a minor tooling change. The finding's claim that it has 'no traceability to the stated intent' is a process/scope concern that doesn't constitute a real defect or important technical issue. The change itself is straightforward and doesn't introduce any correctness, security, or behavioral problems.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:1 — P2, confidence 100: Adding `#!/bin/bash` and a 79-line Tunnelmole/`.env` mutation utility expands the calendar-cache UI/API task into unrelated webhook-development tooling, exposing maintainers to a new environment-changing script that no stated requirement or acceptance criterion justifies.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims the script is 'unrelated' to the PR and 'no stated requirement justifies' it. However, the PR is about Google Calendar cache management, and the script is specifically for testing Google Calendar webhooks (test-gcal-webhooks.sh). This is directly related to the calendar cache functionality being added. The script sets up GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL for local development/testing of the webhook-based cache invalidation. While one could argue about scope, calling it 'unrelated' is inaccurate - it's development tooling for the feature being built. The finding is essentially a scope/architecture opinion presented as a defect, and the claim that it's 'unrelated' is factually incorrect given the Google Calendar context.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/package.json:11 — [P2, confidence 75] `"dev:cron": "npx tsx cron-tester.ts"` executes an undeclared, unpinned package fetched from the npm registry, so a compromised or malicious latest `tsx` release gains arbitrary code execution on a developer machine when this script is run.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows changing from 'ts-node cron-tester.ts' to 'npx tsx cron-tester.ts'. Using npx with an unpinned package means it will fetch the latest version from npm each time if not locally installed. This is a legitimate security concern - if the tsx package were compromised, running this dev script would execute malicious code. However, tsx is a well-known, widely-used TypeScript executor, and this is a dev-only script. The severity is somewhat mitigated by being a development script, but the security concern is technically valid.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:79 — [P1, confidence 100] The purported webhook test ends with only `wait "$TMOLE_PID"` and never invokes or asserts the changed cache-status or cache-deletion behavior, so it stays green or blocks identically when the feature is broken and gives reviewers false verification confidence.

adjudication.rationale: The script is a developer utility for setting up a tunnel for webhook testing, not an automated test that needs assertions. It's a helper script that configures the environment for manual testing. The finding mischaracterizes the purpose of this script - it's infrastructure setup, not a test suite. The script correctly does what it's designed to do: start a tunnel and update the environment variable.
